articles.headline: US Representative Introduces Plan To Preserve Digital Game Ownership
keyFacts: US Representative Ritchie Torres is introducing the Power To The Players Act to secure consumer ownership rights for digital games.
If passed, the legislation would require the Federal Trade Commission to prevent companies from arbitrarily revoking licenses, delisting games, or shutting down servers without offline alternatives.
The bill currently faces regulatory hurdles and has no guarantee of passing.
body: United States Representative Ritchie Torres will introduce the Power To The Players Act. This legislation is being made to support consumers' rights in a way that grants gamers ownership of their digital games. If successful, the Federal Trade Commission could then establish regulations to prevent companies from delisting games, shutting down servers early in a game's life, and easily revoking digital licenses.
Ritchie Torres wants gamers to have ownership of their digital games

Some companies are trying to preserve physical media and keep the disc format alive, but physical games are now endangered. With several publishers no longer selling physical versions, Sony ending disc production, and uncertainty around Project Helix's disc drive, the gaming world is headed towards an all-digital future, and gamers aren't happy.

Regardless of what the future holds for physical games, digital media currently dominates the gaming market. That is why Rep. Ritchie Torres wants to cement gamers' ownership rights over their digital libraries with the introduction of the Power To The Players bill.

At the moment, companies have full control of gamers' digital licenses. Digital storefronts can delist games, cutting off access to a wide audience within seconds. Developers can shut down servers if a game isn't as profitable as they had hoped, stripping gamers of online features promised on launch. As Torres puts it, families use their savings to purchase games, but with a digital license, the software that they paid for can be "pulled out from under them on a company's arbitrary timeline."

If passed, the bill would require the Federal Trade Commission to set regulations that grant consumers ownership of a game and protect their ability to keep playing it. Online games would also have to offer a playable offline mode so fans can keep enjoying the game after servers shut down. It is a bill designed to help players enjoy their games for years to come and to "close the gap between buying a game and owning it."

Right now, the bill still faces plenty of regulatory hurdles, so there's no guarantee it'll see the light of day. Still, it indicates that the United States government is finally taking notice of issues with digital game ownership.

articles.headline: Ember’s new temperature-controlled mug makes my nightly tea ritual even better
keyFacts: Ember released the Mug 3 smart mug and the Tumbler 2, updating its temperature-controlled drinkware lineup.
The Mug 3 includes a physical temperature button, up to three hours of battery life, and top-rack dishwasher safety.
The Mug 3 is available on Ember's website, Target, and Amazon for $129 or $149 depending on size.
body: With the nights getting chillier, I’ve been reaching for a cup of tea more often. And if there’s one thing that can make a cozy fall night even better, it’s a warm drink that actually stays warm. Enter Ember’s new Mug 3, the latest version of the company’s temperature-controlled smart mug, which is designed to keep your drink at just the right temperature for as long as you sip.

Ember first introduced its smart mug in 2016 to solve a problem most coffee and tea drinkers know all too well: getting distracted for a few minutes, only to return to a lukewarm drink. Now, the company is back with its third-generation mug, which brings a handful of practical upgrades.

The biggest change is that you no longer have to open the app to adjust your drink’s temperature. Instead, you can use the button on the bottom of the mug to cycle through five preset temperatures, starting at 125 degrees Fahrenheit. Each press raises the temperature by five degrees, up to a maximum of 145 degrees, so you can easily make your drink a little hotter with each click.

Honestly, this is the feature I ended up using the most during my time testing out the mug. At night, when I’m curled up in bed with a book and a cup of tea, my phone is usually somewhere across the room. Being able to adjust my drink without getting up to find it is a small convenience, but one I genuinely appreciate.
It’s also a welcome change for users who have reported running into connectivity or pairing issues with the Ember app.

That said, I do have one complaint: the button is located on the bottom of the mug. It’s a peculiar design choice when you’re dealing with a cup full of hot liquid, and it isn’t particularly easy to press, either. I often found myself tilting the mug and pressing down firmly to get it to respond. So, while I appreciate the addition of on-mug controls, I wish Ember had made the button easier to reach.

If you prefer using your phone, the Ember app still offers plenty of customization. After pairing the mug with your phone over Bluetooth, you can choose presets based on what you’re drinking. Ember recommends 136 degrees Fahrenheit for black coffee, 132 degrees for green tea, and 142 degrees for lemon water. You can also create your own temperature presets, which is handy if you like your drinks a little hotter or cooler than the recommended settings.

The Mug 3 also comes with a few other upgrades, including a sliding lid designed to help prevent spills. The mug can also keep your drink at its desired temperature for up to three hours on a single charge. And it’s the first mug in Ember’s lineup to be top-rack dishwasher-safe, making cleanup easier. (Just keep in mind that it isn’t microwave-safe.)
The Ember Mug 3 comes in two sizes: a 10-ounce model for $129 and a 14-ounce version for $149.

The smaller mug is available in black, white, and stainless steel, while the larger size comes in eight colors, including sage green, lavender, powder blue, salt blue, sandstone, white, black, and matcha green.

Alongside the new mug, Ember also introduced the Tumbler 2, which replaces both the Travel Mug 2 and the original Tumbler in its lineup. The 16-ounce tumbler features a slimmer, taller design intended to fit standard car cup holders. It’s available in black for $179, while the Travel Mug 2 will remain available until supplies run out.
The products are available to purchase on Ember’s website, Target, and Amazon.

articles.headline: Washington Commanders Rumor Offers MAJOR Update on What Gets Dan Quinn Fired in Week 6
keyFacts: A recent rumor claims head coach Dan Quinn could be fired if the Washington Commanders suffer notable mental lapses or a blowout loss against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 6.
NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that owner Josh Harris dislikes midseason coaching changes and Quinn is expected to coach the rest of the season unless the team quits on him.
Quarterback Jayden Daniels supported Quinn after a late-game clock management error in Week 5, and reports state Quinn maintains strong control of the locker room.
body: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Commanders better not have any notable mental lapses in Week 6, because a new rumor claims it is sure to cost Dan Quinn his job as head coach.

After Washington went 12-5 and reached the NFC Championship Game in the 2024 season, it seemed like the team had found the coach who could make them a consistent playoff contender. However, ever since, the Commanders have regressed.

Last season, they finished with a disappointing 5-12 record. Many chalked it up to injuries — specifically to quarterback Jayden Daniels. However, there were some worrisome signs during the 2025 campaign. It put added pressure on the coach to deliver better results in 2026. However, they are 1-3-1 heading into a Week 6 Monday Night Football clash against the San Francisco 49ers .

Their record is bad, but they seemingly hit a low point in the Quinn era last week when the offense completely lost track of how much time was left on the clock in overtime against the New York Giants and blew a chance at a game-winning field goal.
Washington Commanders would need to be blown out by San Francisco 49ers to fire Dan Quinn

Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Washington Commanders owner Josh Harris poses for a photo with fans before the game between Indianapolis Colts and Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images It has only reignited the discourse about the 56-year-old’s job security and the idea that he could be the first coach fired in-season. However, according to Tom Pelissero, while owner Josh Harris will be “paying close attention” on Monday night, he “ has never been a believer in midseason coaching changes .”

That is why the NFL insider added that unless the Commanders suffer a blowout loss (very possible against a very good 49ers team) or there are obvious signs the team has quit on their coach, “expect Quinn to get the rest of the season to show he can get things turned in the right direction.”
Furthermore, Daniels threw his support behind his coach after he mismanaged their final drive in Week 5, and the NFL insider claims, “Quinn has always had great command of the locker room.”

articles.headline: How big is Russia's threat against Germany?
keyFacts: German domestic intelligence chief Sinan Selen stated that Russia is conducting a long-term hybrid attack against Germany and European allies.
Security expert Nico Lange stated that Germany is heavily targeted because it leads European efforts in supporting Ukraine.
Expert Stefan Meister predicted that Russian drone provocations and attacks on German infrastructure will increase in the coming months.
body: Warnings keep mounting about Russia's threat to Germany. On October 12, Sinan Selen, president of Germany's domestic intelligence agency, the BfV, said that Russia's covert attacks and destabilization efforts against Germany and other European countries are "not a temporary development but a long-term hybrid attack."

Even if the war in Ukraine were to end, said Selen, the Russian threat would not disappear. "For Russia, this is about completely redrawing the map of Europe and redefining its own role within Europe and in global politics."
He added that Russia's aggression would continue to be felt not only in Ukraine, but also in the Baltic states, in Poland and in Germany.
Russia is tied down in Ukraine — for now

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt has described the threat situation as one in which "our country is not at war, but we are the daily target of hybrid warfare." Russia's goal, he said, is not to defeat Germany militarily "but to subdue us politically and socially."

Security experts, however, are not so sure that Russia is only interested in exercising political and social influence. Last year, political scientist Carlo Masala told the political talk show Maischberger that "Russia is preparing for a major war." And he didn't mean just a cyberwar. Inspector General Carsten Breuer, the Bundeswehr's highest-ranking officer, agreed.

For now, though, Russia remains tied up in its war against Ukraine. According to NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, there is no immediate military threat to NATO territory. But according to military experts, European intelligence agencies, and the German Defense Ministry, Russia will have the personnel and equipment to wage a conventional war against NATO by 2029. The Russian defense industry is running at full speed, and Moscow plans to expand its armed forces to 1.5 million soldiers.

At the moment, Russia has other objectives, believes Stefan Meister, an expert on Eastern Europe at the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP): "I don't think Russia has any interest in a direct military conflict with NATO right now. It wants to test NATO and also display its capabilities," he tells DW.
An accidental military confrontation?

An example of Russia's hybrid war might be the failed attack with an explosive-laden drone against a Ukrainian transport aircraft at Leipzig-Halle Airport in August. Soon after, the German government stated that it was certain Russia was behind the attack.
Security expert Nico Lange told DW at the time that Germany was very lucky the explosives did not detonate: "Honestly, it was pure coincidence and not the result of German defensive measures."

As for why Germany was targeted specifically, Lange said: "I believe that Germany has always been a primary target of Russian influence and hybrid warfare. Russia believes that Germany is the key to European decision-making. Germany is now leading the way in supporting Ukraine."

Moscow swiftly responded to the German government's accusation with an angry denial. Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said it was "the beginning of a real war," though there was no immediate further escalation.

Nevertheless, there is always the risk that things could spiral out of control following a Russian provocation and subsequent response, according to Stefan Meister: "Accidentally shooting down an aircraft that they were trying to intimidate would trigger a counter-reaction. But I don't believe that Russia is currently aiming for a direct war but rather for provocations, polarization, and sowing uncertainty among the population."
AfD says less money for Ukraine means more for Germany
Not everyone shares the assessment that Russia poses a threat to Germany — some believe that the threat can be averted.

Despite the war in Ukraine, politicians from the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) and the populist left-wing Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) want to improve relations with Russia, resume Russian energy supplies and end support for Ukraine.

AfD co-leader Tino Chrupalla said in early September, "People are fed up with this escalation against Russia, with the billions being squandered there on a system that is actually funded by German taxpayers' money."

The message appears to have resonated among the population, especially in eastern Germany. The AfD saw strong gains in all three state elections in September. In Saxony-Anhalt, it became the strongest party by far and may even run the government there soon, which would be the first time that a far-right party has held power in Germany since the end of WWII.

The CDU's security policy expert Roderich Kiesewetter disputed the claim made by the AfD and BSW that ending aid to Ukraine would mean greater security and more money for German schools and infrastructure: "Spending on education, social policy, and infrastructure is only possible if we live in freedom and democracy — and, above all, in peace and security. Anyone who believes that we'll have more money for social programs if we stop supporting Ukraine and let Russia have its way is either gravely mistaken or is making themselves a tool of Russian propaganda."
A decades-long pacifist mindset

The perceived security threat has led the German military, the Bundeswehr, to fast-track significant modernization through substantial investment. But it is struggling to find enough recruits for its planned expansion. Many young Germans have taken to the streets to protest against plans to reintroduce conscription. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius faced criticism from inside his own party, the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), for saying that Germany must become "capable of waging war." Many found the statement to be too militaristic.

Is Germany prepared for a military threat? "Not at all. Germany is not well prepared militarily or in the civilian sector, and the population isn't mentally prepared for it either," said Meister. "Just look at the demonstrations against conscription and the military that continue to take place, even though Germany needs a draft. For decades, we've grown up in this culture of pacifism, in a comfort zone. I believe there is very limited societal resilience, but above all, we are not at all mentally prepared for war."

Chancellor Friedrich Merz and his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) are under increasing political pressure — especially from the far right — to scale back support for Ukraine. But Merz never tires of emphasizing that Ukraine will continue to receive support under his chancellorship, calling it a matter of Germany's security. He recently visited Kyiv once again and, together with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, surveyed the destruction caused by Russia.

But this also means that the threat from Russia will continue and even intensify, says Stefan Meister: "I believe we will see a massive increase in attacks such as the one in Leipzig, of provocations involving drones. We will see attacks on infrastructures and possibly also on specific individuals within the military-industrial complex. I believe this is the real, concrete danger facing Germany in the coming months."
This article was translated from German.

articles.headline: Manchester City v Ipswich, Brentford v Liverpool, and more: Football clockwatch - live
keyFacts: Chelsea beat Everton 2-0 to move into fourth place in the Premier League.
Lewis-Potter scored to put Brentford 1-0 up against Liverpool, who lost half-time substitute Frimpong to an injury.
Ipswich equalized against Manchester City through Maeda in the 21st minute to make the score 1-1.
body: Thriller of the day: Kilmarnock were 1-0 up against Motherwell in the second minute, 2-1 down in the 56th, and they’ve just gone 3-2 up! Also in Scotland, Queen of the South have got on the scoresheet and now trail by just the four goals, 1-5 down at home to goal-crazy Ross County.

“In some regards, Frimpong reminds me of Reece James, and not in a good way,” writes Joe Pearson. “Seems like every time he gets on the pitch, the next shot we see of him is sitting down getting ready to be subbed off for injury. He appears to have a lot of potential, but we never get to see it. Sigh.” Today has been pretty ugly for him, very much putting the pong into Frimpong. Another layoff beckons.
Liverpool are being forced into another substitution – and the half-time substitute Frimpong is going off again! His six-minute cameo is over, and Rio Ngumoha is on!

Frimpong, with one of his first touches, pushes the ball down the right flank and takes on Sepp van den Berg for pace. It should be easy, against a lumbering 6ft 4in centre-half, but Van den Berg wins the race.

Liverpool are making a halftimely change, with Frimpong coming on. Brentford are going to make two. Thanks to all that first-half stoppage time they’re yet to get back going there (while Fulham, who only had a single added minute at the end of the first half, are already 10 minutes into their second half).

Second halves are ongoing and goals already flying in: the league-doubling department has seen Birmingham go 2-0 up at home to QPR (Liam Millar with the goal) and Salford 2-0 up at home to Crawley (Macaulay Langstaff).

A brief half-time report from voluntary Scotland correspondent Simon McMahon: “Goals for every team in the Scottish Premier at half time, Simon, apart of course from Dundee United who, despite enjoying the better of the first 45, trail 1-0 at St. Johnstone. Elsewhere it’s Aberdeen 1-1 St. Mirren, Hibs 1-2 Falkirk and Motherwell 1-1kilmarnock. And Ross County have five at the break.”

“Hello Simon,” writes Kári Tulinius. Hello to you!. “To my admittedly amateur eyes, Manchester City haven’t been playing very well, with Ipswich clearly the better team. However, City have plenty of players who can create chances out of nothing, and forwards who can score from very little. That’s what shopping with with a bottomless purse buys you.” Not playing very well, perhaps, but certainly doing enough to be deservedly ahead. But as to how they’re doing it, yes that helps.
Because of Szoboszlai’s injury they were anyway playing six minutes of stoppage time at Brentford, and with that VAR delay they’re now in the 55th minute of the first half, and still going.

Yehor Yarmoliuk is sent off! Darren England, the VAR, took an age to pick up on the foul, but got there in the end. There was not a lot to it, and Jacquet certainly made the most of it, but there was definitely aggressive movement there, and I suppose that’s enough.
Handbags! Jeremy Jacquet goes down inside the Brentford penalty area as a corner comes in, and it looks like there might have been a headbutt there from Yarmoliuk!
The whistle blows at Craven Cottage, where Fulham have been completely dominant: 79% possession, 10-2 ahead on shots, 25-3 up on touches in the opposition box.
GOAL! Brentford 1-0 Liverpool (Lewis-Potter, 44 mins)
And now Liverpool are behind! It’s just an excellent cross and an excellent header from Potter, who has ghosted unmarked into the heart of the area from midfield.

It’s Dango Ouattara, who dives at the ball and somehow contrives to backheel it away from Mac Allister! The players then come together, and the Argentinian goes down, and given the speed at which it all happens it’s an understandable decision in the moment. It’s also an easy intervention for VAR and precisely the kind of decision that’s there to deal with.

At Brentford, Wirtz goes down in the area with a defender’s arm across him, as he tries to spin onto a ball that was probably hit too firmly for him anyway. It’s not nothing, but nor is it enough. Play on.

A precious lead for Fulham! A nice finish from the edge of the area, teed up by Berge, though Hull certainly contributed – they give the ball away inside their own area with a mishit clearance, and then the goalkeeper dives over the shot in a way that looks extremely clumsy.

At Brentford, Barcola is booked for pulling back Kayode. Very little contact there, though, and I’m far from certain it was even a free kick. Worse still for Liverpool, Szoboszlai is on the ground and looking grumpy, and they’re preparing a substitution.
GOAL! Manchester City 1-1 Ipswich (Maeda, 21 mins)
Ipswich equalise within moments! Maeda holds off the defender, convinces Donnarumma that he’s going to shoot towards the far post and instead passes inside the near!

Meanwhile Liverpool really should be in the lead at Brenford: Barcola runs clean through on goal, and has all sorts of time and space to draw the keeper and choose how to finish, but he shoots the wrong side of the post!

West Brom may have started the day above Blackburn in the Championship table but they’re below them now: Andri Gudjohnsen has scored twice in the first 12 minutes and Blackburn are currently in the top eight!

Here’s the Scottish League One table, while there isn’t much else to chat about. Today the team with the worst goal difference (Queen of the South on -19 having conceded 29) is up against the team with the best (Ross County’s +29 having scored 33), so this kind of outcome was pretty predictable.

Mismatch of the day contender: In Scottish League One, Ross County are 3-0 up at Queen of the South with only 10 minutes played. Ross County have a +29 goal difference after nine-and-a-ninth completed games
8 mins: Early days yet, but Liverpool have had their first shot of the day, Szoboszlai completely skying a first-time effort from the edge of the area.
Ollie Arblaster has scored the first goal in the Championship’s 3pm kick-offs, putting Sheffield United one up at Bristol City. A “controlled strike from the edge of the box”, apparently.
Andy Hunter’s match report from the Hill Dickinson is here, and you can find it below.

Chelsea have returned from the international break with an authority that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. A brace from Pedro Neto condemned Everton to an inaugural defeat of the season as the visitors climbed to fourth on the back of their first Premier League clean sheet since January. A head injury sustained by Emi Martínez, who was carried off on a stretcher after seven minutes of treatment, was the only concern from a mature display in the Merseyside sunshine for Alonso’s team.

There were goalkeeping issues at both ends of the field with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in succession as David Moyes’ side suffered self-inflicted wounds. But Everton could have no complaints about the merits of Chelsea’s victory given their contrasting performances in the second half.
A pre-match missive from Billy Munday, our actual correspondent at Craven Cottage!

Fulham and Hull have emerged from the cottage at, er, Craven Cottage with the home side and their manager in particular need of a positive result. Fulham are one of three remaining teams in the Premier League without a win and that means Álvaro Arbeloa is under increasing pressure since his appointment in the summer. This fixture is the second of three of Fulham’s triple header against the promoted sides, having surrendered a lead in the dying minutes at Ipswich last Saturday. It’s a full house.

Voluntary Scotland correspondent Simon McMahon gets in touch: “Hi Simon,” he writes. articles.headline: Why isn't Nico lamaleava playing for UCLA? Bruins QB out for season after injury
keyFacts: UCLA starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava is out for the remainder of the season due to a knee injury he suffered against Oregon.
The injury forces the undefeated Bruins to adjust their offense without their key passer as they prepare to play Wisconsin.
Head coach Bob Chesney indicated that Cal Poly transfer Ty Dieffenbach will get an opportunity to start against Wisconsin.
body: The 12th-ranked UCLA football team is off to an impressive start under head coach Bob Chesney. But the Bruins will have to continue without starting quarterback Nico lamaleava. The former five-star quarterback is out for the remainder of the season after suffering a knee injury in UCLA's victory over Oregon last week.

The injury is a significant setback for the undefeated Bruins, who entered the week with a 5-0 record. With unprecedented postseason hopes on the line, UCLA must now adjust its offense as it prepares to face Wisconsin on Saturday.

Iamaleava injured his left knee late in the second quarter against Oregon. He was tackled by Bear Alexander and Jerry Mixon while scrambling, with his leg appearing to twist during the play. UCLA's medical staff attended to the quarterback, who returned for one more play and threw an interception. However, he did not return to the field after halftime and was later seen without his uniform.
Although UCLA had not officially confirmed his status earlier this week, Chesney acknowledged there was "serious concern" about the quarterback's condition.

Iamaleava's absence leaves a significant gap in UCLA's offense. His ability to extend plays has helped the Bruins escape difficult situations, while his mobility forces opposing defenses to account for the passing game. This also creates opportunities for the rushing attack. He finishes the season with 982 passing yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions on 72-of-116 passing. He also recorded 144 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.

UCLA has two possible replacements for Iamaleava. Cal Poly transfer Ty Dieffenbach and Nico's younger brother, Madden lamaleava. Dieffenbach replaced the injured starter against Oregon, completing three of six passes for 43 yards and a touchdown.
Chesney indicated that Dieffenbach would get an opportunity to start against Wisconsin.

articles.headline: Ukraine still can't intercept drones due to Starlink issues, Zelenskyy says
keyFacts: President Zelenskyy said Starshield speed restrictions prevent Ukraine from using the satellite technology to intercept Russian drones.
Donald Trump and Elon Musk both denied responsibility for imposing speed limits on Ukraine's Starshield systems.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine is discussing restrictions with U.S. officials and will no longer avoid striking Russian refineries.
body: Ukraine is against Russian drones, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday, because of speed restrictions imposed on Starshield, an upgraded military version of Elon Musk's Starlink, amid an ongoing row with President Trump.

"Unfortunately, we can't use Starlink or Starshield technology on our territory today to shoot down jet-powered Shaheds," Zelenskyy said in an online group chat with reporters at the EU Summit. "They fly, and we can stop them with aircraft and other air defense, but we don't use Starlink for that, unfortunately. God willing, this will be restored."

Zelenskyy said Kyiv was discussing the issue with U.S. officials, and he was told the restrictions were linked to technical issues. The Ukrainian president added, however, that Starlink appears to be operating at higher speeds on European Union territory.

"Yes, we are in dialogue at the level of the military, the Ministry of Defense and diplomats, in touch with everyone including SpaceX. Nobody there is answering our military or the Ministry of Defense now," Zelenskyy said. "At various levels they say these are technical problems."

"Here (in Ukraine) Starlink works up to a speed of 161 km/h, then shuts off," he continued. "In the EU it works at 180-plus and works constantly. Here it shuts off in the second minute after 161 km/h and stops working. We lose both drones and connectivity."
Mr. Trump he had not limited Ukraine's access to Starlink, adding he didn't believe Musk, SpaceX's CEO, was responsible either.

"Well, I don't know if it was anybody because it wasn't me, and I don't think it was Elon," Mr. Trump said while leaving the White House to travel for a rally in Georgia. "And from what I understand, it's the same as it's always been."

Musk said Wednesday he isn't responsible for deciding how Starshield is used, writing on X: "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS."
Starshield is to Ukraine's armed forces as it allows personnel to communicate and carry out strikes, including by maintaining contact with drones across long distances.

On Saturday, Zelenskyy said Russia carried out a large attack on Ukraine's energy sector, targeting more than 15 critical power generation and transmission facilities across the country. A day earlier, the president said the current restrictions on Starshield had left people vulnerable to Russian drones, which was "very painful and frustrating"

Ukrainian officials and soldiers the country's military began experiencing sudden difficulties with Starshield equipment late Tuesday, including speed limits that made it more difficult to carry out missions with fast-moving drones. Sources in said SpaceX had unilaterally imposed the Starshield restrictions.

Mr. Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Zelenskyy in recent days, blaming the war between Russia and Ukraine for high global energy prices. The Trump administration on buying Russian diesel last week in an effort to ease pressure, a move Zelenskyy argued could embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.

In a social media post on Saturday, Zelenskyy called the move "unfortunate," adding the act, championed by late Sen. Lindsey Graham, "could have helped enormously." Later, he told journalists he believed the Trump administration will lift more sanctions on Russia.
"Unfortunately, the lifting of sanctions will continue. I believe the 'diesel deal' is just the first step," Zelenskyy told reporters. CBS News has reached out to the White House for comment.

Mr. Trump had agreed to stop striking each other's energy infrastructure — announcing an "energy ceasefire" over the weekend. Zelenskyy Ukraine was willing to abide by such an agreement, but that Russia's strikes never ceased, and several days later he told the Financial Times his country would no longer hold off on striking Russian refineries because Russia was still attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
The Russian government never confirmed it had agreed to a ceasefire.

In a Newsmax interview late Thursday, Mr. Trump called Zelenskyy "not a good guy for us to deal with," argued Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries would be a "disgrace," urged both sides to make a deal and said the Ukrainian leader is harder to deal with than Putin.
"I'm not a big fan of Zelenskyy," Mr. Trump said.
On Wednesday, Musk had tweeted: "Time for Zelensky to go."

articles.headline: Glasgow get bonus-point win at emotion-filled Sale
keyFacts: Glasgow Warriors defeated Sale Sharks 47-27 in an Investec Champions Cup match at CorpAcq Stadium, following an emotional pre-match minute's silence for former Sale lock Hyron Andrews.
Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson stated that the team came together through the trauma of Andrews' death on Friday.
In the second round of fixtures in December, Glasgow will host Pau and Sale will travel to face Leinster.
body: - Published
Investec Champions Cup
Sale Sharks (15) 27
Tries: B Curry, Reed 2, Ma'asi-White Cons: Ford 2 Pen: Ford
Glasgow Warriors (21) 47
Tries: Penalty try, Steyn, Dobie, Craig, Darge, Smith, Tuipulotu Cons: Horne 4, Lancaster
Glasgow Warriors pulled away to record an impressive bonus-point victory over Sale Sharks in the Investec Champions Cup at an emotional CorpAcq Stadium.

Pre-match tears were shed on the pitch and in the stands during a minute's silence in memory of former Sale lock Hyron Andrews, who died on Friday at the Johannesburg Lions' team hotel ahead of their Champions Cup match at La Rochelle.
The 31-year-old played regularly for Sale last season, and his former side started positively as they sought a memorable performance.
Ben Curry peeled off a maul and sprinted through, much to Glasgow's surprise, before Arron Reed crossed out wide after some sharp handling.
However, a penalty try for a maul infringement sent Gus Warr to the sin-bin, before Tom Roebuck joined him after tripping Warriors captain Kyle Steyn.
After Rory Darge spilled the ball with a try beckoning, Glasgow finally took advantage as Steyn raced down the wing to score.
A wonderful finish by Scotland's Jamie Dobie regained the visitors' lead after George Ford's penalty had put Sale back ahead.
Considered one of the favourites to win the tournament after recording a clean sweep of bonus-point wins in last year's pool stage, Glasgow were stunned by Toulon in the quarter-finals at Scotstoun.
One of those wins came against Sale after Franco Smith's side recovered from 14 points down to win 26-21.
Lock Alex Craig powered over from close range as a similar pattern began to emerge, with Rekeiti Ma'asi-White crossing after sustained pressure to keep Alex Sanderson's side in touch.
A sublime one-handed offload from Joe Carpenter then set up Reed to respond to a Warriors maul try.
However, Smith's side, who will be aiming for a deep run in Europe, crossed through replacement Ollie Smith and Ottavio Tuipulotu to secure an additional bonus point.
A new rule in this year's tournament awards an extra point to teams that score three more tries than their opponents.
The second round of fixtures in the Champions Cup will be played in December, with Glasgow hosting Pau and Sale travelling to Dublin to face Leinster.
Andrews' death 'still really raw to process' - Sanderson

Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live about the death of former Sharks player Hyron Andrews: "I am really impressed with how the lads have come together, looked after each other and got tighter in the trauma of it.
"It is a good indication of the strength of the squad and the depth of the culture, how much they want to get around each other and get through it together.
"Hyron represents a large portion of the squad, in that he came here underrated and got opportunities to show what he is capable of.
"He forwarded his career, made Manchester his second home, settled with his wife and had another child.

"He left with a lot of good mates and people who consider him as one of their best mates. His impact and what he gave off the field was far more from what he gave on it. It is still really raw to process.
"His two boys are too young to really fathom what is going on but I know the lads close to Hyron have been speaking to his two boys already this morning.
"We will help their family get through it.
"It was not something we looked to use or to weaponise. I'd never want to do that because I think you would kind of be dishonouring him.
"You can ride emotion and some of them wanted to do right by Hyron today. They have to get through it in their own time and way - that is grief.
"Collectively we can grieve together and be there for each other. I imagine they found it hard. I found it hard, trying to come in and be my positive self.
"They didn't really show it with how they started. It shows the pros they are."
Glasgow flanker Rory Darge, speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live: "Sale are a really good side, especially their pack. That was a challenge we set our pack. I thought we did really well at the set piece.
"We will enjoy this as we know how tough Sale are to beat here."

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
keyFacts: Pope Leo XIV left the hospital Saturday following surgery that removed part of his right lung, his doctors said.
Examination of the removed tissue confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, according to the pope's doctors.
Doctors expect the pope to lead Sunday prayers, while his office has cleared his public schedule until at least Oct. 20.
body: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery

Pope Leo XIV left Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday afternoon and returned to the Vatican after doctors said he was well enough to be discharged following surgery that removed part of his right lung.

The Vatican press office released a statement outlining details from Dr. Luigi Carbone,the Pope's personal physician, and Professor Stefano Margaritora, Gemelli's chief of thoracic surgery who led the team that operated on Leo. The two doctors said the pope had undergone blood tests and a chest X-ray that morning, with the results confirming his clinical condition meant he could leave hospital.

They said he was expected to lead the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment on Sunday.Video showed Leo waving to well-wishers outside the hospital as he walked out without physical support, flanked by officials and security guards in dark suits.
Before leaving, the pope had celebrated Mass in a room set aside for that purpose on the hospital's 10th floor, according to the press office.

Vatican spokesperson Matteo Bruni said "the estimated post-operative recovery time will be about one week." Leo's discharge came on his fifth day in hospital and was sooner than had been expected at the time of the operation's announcement.
A diagnosis made public
Leo, 71, had told crowds in St. Peter's Square last Sunday that doctors had discovered a "localized nodule" in his lung at a "very early stage."
"Following their advice, I have therefore decided to undergo an operation to remove it," he said.

The surgery on Tuesday went further than the nodule, however, with surgeons using a video-assisted technique to remove the lower lobe of the pope's right lung in an operation that lasted about 90 minutes. His doctors said lung tissue examined afterward confirmed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. With adenocarcinoma making up about 40% of all lung cancers in the U.S., it is the nation's most common form of lung cancer, according to the Lung Cancer Foundation of America.
That is true among nonsmokers too, according to Dr. Otis Brawley, an oncologist at Johns Hopkins University and former chief medical and scientific officer of the American Cancer Society.

Leo is not known to have smoked, but cancer does run in his family. His mother, Mildred, died of cancer in 1990, and on Tuesday the Vatican announced that his older brother Louis, who lives in Florida, has been hospitalized with a form of cancer.
Encouraging signs
Doctors not involved in the pope's care say the treatment so far points to a cancer that has been caught early.

"The fact that surgery was the first tool that they utilized is a really good sign," Dr. Vin Gupta, a pulmonologist and board member of the American Lung Association, told NPR. "It suggests that they think this is early stage."

Gupta said the fact that doctors removed a larger portion of the lung than first announced is not in itself a bad sign. "People have parts of their lungs removed all the time for all sorts of reasons, and they recover just fine," he said. "And in his case, he's pretty robust at baseline from a health standpoint."
Leo still exercises regularly, playing tennis each week with his personal secretary and riding horses at Castel Gandolfo, the papal retreat to the south of Rome.
The Vatican has not announced any further treatment.
Travels ahead

Leo's office has cleared his public schedule until at least Oct. 20. His next major international trip, set for early November, includes Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he lived on and off for two decades and holds citizenship.

"He had a minimally invasive surgery," said Dr. Jonathan Villena Vargas, a cardiothoracic surgeon at Weill Cornell Medical Center in New York City. "Because we do this all the time, most patients are allowed to travel about two weeks after the surgery."

Brawley from Johns Hopkins agreed. "I think he can do it," he said, adding that patients in good physical shape who have this type of procedure "very frequently are back to normal in seven to 10 days."

articles.headline: Richarlison takes aim at Roberto De Zerbi on social media in fresh swipe at Tottenham boss
keyFacts: Tottenham player Richarlison used social media to agree with former coach Duncan Ferguson that he has been unfairly treated by manager Roberto De Zerbi.
Richarlison has been omitted from Tottenham's Premier League squad and is in the final year of his contract.
The earliest Richarlison could feature for Tottenham is in the FA Cup in January, though his contract expires at the end of the season.
body: Richarlison has risked further tension with Roberto De Zerbi after taking aim at the Tottenham boss on social media.
The 29-year-old has been frozen out at Spurs having been omitted from the De Zerbi’s Premier League squad .
Richarlison, who has been on Tottenham’s books since 2022, is in the final year of his contract AFP
The decision came after the Brazilian started in the north London outfit’s opening game of the top-flight campaign – a 3-0 defeat away at Brentford.
A move back to Everton then fell through in the closing stages of the summer transfer window.
Richarlison has already taken to social media to express his pain over his continued exile.
And he has now taken to his Instagram to respond to comments made by Everton icon Duncan Ferguson – who coached him at Goodison Park.
What did Duncan Ferguson say about Richarlison?
Speaking on the Overlap Daily, the Scotsman stressed the forward doesn’t deserve the treatment he has been subject to.
He remarked: “I don’t know what the manager [ De Zerbi ] at Tottenham’s done, I don’t know if they’ve had a massive fall-out, and knowing Richy they probably have.
“But you’ve got to put your arm around him and say, ‘Come on, Richy,’ and get him back in.
“You don’t leave a player like that out (of the squad) unless there’s been a real murder – he’s chinned him, or there’s been a proper scrap on the training ground.
“Richarlison’s a good player, and Tottenham are not that great, are they?
“It’s all hands-on deck. You need all your assets out there. The manager knows what he’s doing, he’s on the ground, but Richarlison’s a great player and I enjoyed working with him.”
Richarlison agreed with Ferguson’s view that he has been unfairly treated by De Zerbi Instagram
How did Richarlison hit out at De Zerbi?
A shortened segment of Ferguson’s words were posted on X, with Richarlison sharing the snippet on his Instagram story.
Issuing a brief six-word statement, he agreed that he has been unfairly treated by De Zerbi.
He simply said: “Thanks Duncan Ferguson, you are right.”
What’s next for Richarlison?
With Spurs already dumped out of the Carabao Cup and not competing in Europe, the earliest Richarlison could feature for the club would be in the FA Cup in January.
But with his contract to expire at the end of the season, he may have already played his last game for Spurs.
After being denied a move to Everton, a transfer to return to his homeland to join Vasco de Gama then failed to come to fruition .
Richarlison finished as Spurs’ top scorer last season with 12 goals, but was deemed as surplus to requirements by De Zerbi Getty
The ex-Watford man failed to agree terms with the Brazilian outfit, who had agreed a deal in principle to sign him.
In an attempt to force through a move away from Spurs, Richarlison approached FIFA last month in an attempt to terminate his contract .

articles.headline: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
keyFacts: Meta removed language from its commercial terms that suggested the company could scrape content from websites to train its artificial intelligence.
Experts interpreted the removed terms as an attempt by Meta to train AI using scraped website content and bypass robots.txt instructions.
Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts stated that the crawling terms applied only to ads and business products, not scraping news sites.
body: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page:
Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

… Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

Andy Stone, Meta’s vice president of communications, and spokesperson Daniel Roberts pushed back, saying that “There is no change to how Meta uses web crawlers; any suggestion to the contrary is false.” Today’s update to its terms and a new statement go further, removing the controversial language entirely. Roberts said in a follow-up statement to The Verge this morning:

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

articles.headline: Vance publicly hints at his disagreement with Trump over Iran war
keyFacts: Vice President JD Vance publicly hinted that he has disagreed with President Donald Trump over the Iran war.
Vance said he persistently questions the strategic goals, costs, and trade-offs of the military conflict within the White House.
A CBS town hall interview featuring Vance discussing the administration's economic challenges is scheduled to air over the weekend.
body: Vice President JD Vance on Friday publicly hinted at breaking with President Donald Trump over the Iran war , signaling a split at the White House as the conflict approaches the eight-month mark.
Vance made the comments during an interview on the Sean Spicer Show , when he was pressed on media personality Tucker Carlson’s attacks on Trump over the war.
“Even if you disagree with him on that one issue, you can have that disagreement. And I think I have had that disagreement,” Vance said of the debate on the Iran war.

Carlson was known in conservative circles for years, but has leaned into more socialist-leaning populism in recent months with weighty critiques of the Trump administration. Though he and Vance remain friends, Carlson recently offered a tacit endorsement to Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul el Sayed , whom Republicans are furiously fighting to defeat in November with GOP candidate Mike Rogers . El Sayed is very critical of the Iran war and Israel , topics where Carlson is also strongly critical of the Trump administration, setting him at odds with the White House.
Vance admonished Carlson during the Spicer interview, saying he’s told the media personality not to “throw the baby out with the bathwater.

“When Tucker says, for instance, that ‘Abdul el Sayed is the America First candidate,’ what I’d say to Tucker again — I said this to him privately, and I’ll say it publicly — ‘Okay, Abdul el Sayed is a guy who you agree with him about the Iran war, and I understand that. But wait a second, this is a guy who says that the Iran conflict is a problem because it violates international law,’” Vance said. “How was that America first?”
The vice president said he and Trump are “aligned” on the war. But Vance conceded that the role he plays within the White House is one of persistently questioning the rationale for the conflict.

“You can’t just go to war because it feels good,” he said. You can’t go to war because you’re angry or because you’re frustrated. You have to say, ‘What does this military objective — how is it connected to a strategic goal that we have for the United States of America?’

“And that is certainly the role that I play within the Oval Office. I’m always asking: ‘If we do this thing, how does it accomplish something that we care about? What are the costs and benefits? What are the trade-offs here?’”
Before becoming Trump’s vice president, Vance represented Ohio in the U.S. Senate , where he was known for his largely non-interventionist, isolationist-leaning foreign policy stance.

Since becoming Trump’s No. 2, the White House has leaned on Vance to articulate the government’s rationale for the war in Iran and other issues challenging the administration, such as the economy, to skeptical voters, particularly ahead of the midterm elections.
Economic issues have proved increasingly challenging for Republicans to navigate, due to energy prices that have surged due to the Iran war.

In a CBS town hall interview set to air over the weekend, Vance suggested some of the economic issues were inherited from the Biden administration. He conceded that it could take a while for Trump to turn around the economy, but expressed confidence the president could do so.

articles.headline: Common problems with Amazon Alexa and how to fix them
keyFacts: Engadget reported that common Amazon Alexa issues can be resolved through straightforward settings adjustments and troubleshooting steps.

Unresponsive or buggy Alexa devices can be fixed by unmuting, restarting the hardware or router, or checking for software updates.
body: Common problems with Amazon Alexa and how to fix them
Some of the most common Alexa problems have very easy solutions.

Utilizing Alexa has become increasingly accessible since its release, with heaps of different Echo Dots and Shows to choose from alongside accessories like the Echo Auto and Echo Buds. You don't even need a physical device to access the service anymore with the new rollout of Alexa+. With so much proliferation, however, comes more and more room for things to go wrong.

At this point, it's entirely possible to design an entire smart home built on the back of Alexa. You can control your lights, sound systems, television, and security system all in one place, and set Routines to make them all work day-to-day with minimal effort. Of course, this doesn't come without downsides — aside from concerns surrounding the fact that Alexa is technically always listening, if you're reliant on Alexa, small common problems can have a big impact. Thankfully, they've also got easy solutions.
Fixes for common Alexa problems
If your Alexa doesn't understand you
If your Alexa doesn't seem to understand your voice, try setting up a Voice ID:
- Open the Alexa app.
- Select More, then Settings.
- Select Account Management and select your profile.
- Select Voice ID and follow the instructions.
You can also say, "Alexa, learn my voice" to the same effect.
If your Alexa is too talkative

If your Alexa's long-winded responses have become a bother, there are a couple of different methods you can try: Brief Mode and changing her personality type to Brief. The latter is one of several Alexa personality settings and will edit out things like filler statements while still speaking to you. The former is even more concise, often changing what would typically be a verbal response into a short sound cue to let you know you've been heard.
To turn on Brief personality:
- Open the Alexa app.
- Open Devices.
- Select your device, then select Settings.
- Select Alexa's Personality Style and choose Brief.
To turn on Brief Mode:
- Open the Alexa app.
- Select More, then Settings.
- Select Voice Responses.
- Turn Brief Mode on.
Both of these settings can also be enabled verbally by saying, "Alexa, enable Brief Mode" or "Alexa, change your personality style to Brief."
If your Alexa keeps waking to random words
If normal conversation keeps activating your Alexa, try changing your Wake Word to something less common:
- Open the Alexa app.
- Select Devices, then select your device.
- Select Device Settings, then Wake Word.
- Choose a new Wake Word and hit OK.
You can also say, "Alexa, change your Wake Word." Unfortunately, the Wake Word can't be customized and must be chosen from a list.
If Alexa is playing from the wrong speaker

If you have multiple Alexas and it's playing music or other sounds through the wrong one, it's worth placing your devices into Groups based on the room they're in. Then, you can say things like, "Alexa, play music in the bedroom," to ensure the right speaker. To set up Groups:
- Open the Alexa app.
- Select Devices.
- At the top, where you can find Groups, select New Group, then tap Create a room or device group and follow the prompts to customize the Group.
Tips for a buggy Alexa

Sometimes, an Alexa can just be completely unresponsive. If your Alexa can't seem to hear you, it's first worthwhile to try to eliminate other loud noises that might be causing interference. If that doesn't work, make sure that your Alexa isn't muted by checking for a solid red light (a ring of light on speaker devices or a red bar with a mute icon on screen devices). To unmute the device, find the mute button, which is typically on the top or side of the device, and press it to unmute.

If muting wasn't the cause, the next best course of action is a simple restart, which can be done by unplugging the device for a few seconds, then plugging it back in — this solution applies to other issues like general lag or freezing, too. It's also possible the problem is related to a poor Wi-Fi connection, which could be solved by restarting your router via the same unplug method. Sometimes, though, bugginess is something that has a software root cause. It's always worth checking for a software update by saying, "Alexa, check for software updates." If there is one, the device will automatically update, hopefully solving the issue.

articles.headline: Thousands rally for biggest protest in years against Tunisia’s Saied
keyFacts: Thousands of Tunisians marched in Tunis on Saturday in the largest protest in years against President Kais Saied.
The rally was led by the UGTT trade union alongside civil society groups and opposition parties.
Protesters demanded the release of detained critics amid worsening living conditions and restrictions on political freedoms.
body: Thousands of Tunisians have marched through the capital to protest against President Kais Saied, worsening living conditions and restrictions on political freedoms.
The latest demonstration in Tunis on Saturday was led by the Tunisian General Labour Union (UGTT), an influential trade union federation, alongside opposition parties and civil society organisations.
It was the largest protest against Saied in years, bringing together political opponents whose longstanding divisions have weakened their ability to challenge his rule.
The AFP news agency reported that more than 3,000 people were on the march, but the total could not be independently confirmed.
Protesters gathered along Habib Bourguiba Avenue, a major street in central Tunis, as hundreds of police deployed across the capital. Several surrounding roads were closed.

The crowd included lawyers, doctors, journalists and the unemployed, as well as activists and members of parties from across the political spectrum. They demanded the release of detained government critics and an end to restrictions on trade union rights.
Placards reading “No democracy without freedoms” and “No dignity with poverty” reflected the political and economic grievances driving the demonstration.
Protesters also revived a slogan demanding the government’s removal, widely heard during Tunisia’s 2011 uprising.
Addressing the rally on Saturday, UGTT leader Salah Eddine Salmi criticised the concentration of political power in the presidency and said “silence will no longer be acceptable”.
The political demands came alongside mounting frustration over the cost of basic goods and declining purchasing power.
Prolonged difficulties
Tunisia has struggled with prolonged economic difficulties, deteriorating public services, recurring water and electricity cuts, as well as shortages of medicines and other essentials.
Demonstrator Yassine Gharseli, who travelled from Sfax, about 250km south of Tunis, said repeated disruptions to basic services had deepened his frustration with the authorities.
“I came from Sfax to stand up for my freedom,” he told the Reuters news agency at the demo, expressing his determination to continue speaking out.
Saturday’s march followed other demonstrations over similar grievances.
On August 20 , protesters in Tunis rallied against rising prices and shortages of basic goods.
Last month, fuel transport workers went on a two-day strike over wages and working conditions, led by a union federation affiliated with the UGTT.
The demands recall the uprising that ousted longtime President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali in 2011, which helped ignite protests across the Arab world.
Tunisia subsequently held competitive elections and expanded political freedoms, but unemployment and struggling public services remain persistent sources of anger.

Saied came to power promising an alternative to that political system; however, in 2021, he suspended parliament and dismissed the government, saying he was confronting corruption and political deadlock.
He later dissolved parliament and a new constitution increased presidential powers in 2022.

articles.headline: Trump traveling to Kentucky to rally supporters ahead of midterms
keyFacts: President Trump is traveling to Kentucky on Saturday to rally supporters and aid Republicans in competitive midterm races.
The visit matters because Republicans are defending narrow majorities in both the Senate and the House.
Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear said that Trump campaigning in the state suggests Republicans are in big trouble.
body: President Trump is heading to Kentucky Saturday to rally supporters and shore up Republicans facing unexpectedly competitive races — including a House contest that could put another seat at risk for the GOP.

Trump’s trip to Highland Heights, in Northern Kentucky, also puts him just across the Ohio River from battleground Ohio, where former US Sen. Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio) is trying to reclaim his seat from US Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), who was appointed to fill the vacancy left by Vice President JD Vance.

Trump has visited Ohio four times during his current term, including two trips this month. During one visit, he joked about examining Husted’s backside — a reminder of the state’s importance as Republicans fight to preserve their 53-47 Senate majority and narrow 218-214 House majority.
The race is considered a pure tossup, in a state Trump carried against former Vice President Kamala Harris 55-44 in 2024, according to the Cook Political Report.
Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear, a potential 2028 presidential candidate, said Trump’s decision to campaign in a state he won handily was a troubling sign for Republicans.

“I don’t take any vote for granted” he told reporters this week. “But the fact that in the weeks leading up to this midterm election, the president’s coming to a state he won by 31 points that he believes he needs, suggest to me that Republicans are in big trouble,” he said, slightly padding Trump’s 30-point 2016 victory.

Trump’s rally also gives him access to Ohio television markets and a chance to demonstrate loyalty to a congressional candidate, Ed Gallrein, he helped push through a primary by opposing the incumbent, said University of Kentucky political scientist Stephen Voss.
It also puts Trump within reach of another congressional district where Republicans face a tougher fight, Voss said.
Rep. Andy Barr (R-Ky.) is hoping to fill Sen. Mitch McConnell’s (R-Ky.) seat, and is battling Democratic state Rep. Charles Booker.

A Global Strategy Group poll released by Booker’s campaign Sept. 9 had him trailing 49-40, with a margin of error of 4%. McConnell, 84, has occasionally bedeviled Trump, even while pushing through his court nominees and being sidelined by health challenges.

Barr’s Senate bid has opened up a House seat in the Lexington area, about a 90-minute drive from Trump’s rally. Democrat Zach Dembo, a former Navy JAG officer who left his job as a federal prosecutor in the Trump Justice Department, is challenging Republican Ralph Alvarado, a former state health commissioner.
The Cook Political Report moved the district Oct. 9 from “safe Republican” to the more competitive “leans Republican” category.

Republicans are favored in the state’s 4th Congressional District, where Trump helped knock off Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) in the primary, calling him a “nutjob”. Now, primary winner Ed Gallrein, a retired Navy SEAL, is taking on Democrat businesswoman Melissa Strange. Gallrein is favored, but some younger voters and indepdnents are threatening to stay home.
“Every once in a while you see a case where the electorate is angered so much that they sit on their hands,” said Voss.
Analysts say persistent inflation, the Iran war, and fuel costs have made races competitive across the country even in Republican-leaning territory.
Trump’s trip followed visits to Alaska, Montana, and Georgia this week.
