articles.headline: Elon Musk agrees to settle lawsuits over 2024 election lottery
keyFacts: Elon Musk and America PAC agreed to settle two lawsuits alleging they defrauded voters with a daily million-dollar giveaway before the 2024 election.
Arizona plaintiffs claimed Musk and America PAC misled voters in seven swing states into signing a petition supporting the US Constitution.
The settlements are subject to court approval, and the court filings did not include the settlement terms.
body: Elon Musk and his America Pac political action committee said recently that they agreed to settle two proposed class actions alleging the billionaire entrepreneur defrauded residents in closely contested states before the 2024 US election by promising voters a lottery-style daily $1m giveaway.
The plaintiffs, Musk and America Pac told the judge overseeing the two related lawsuits in federal court in Austin, Texas, on Thursday that they have reached settlements subject to court approval.
The filings did not include settlement terms, and lawyers involved in the case declined to comment or did not respond to requests for more information.

The plaintiffs in the two cases are Arizona residents who said Musk and America Pac misled voters in seven swing states into signing his petition to support the US constitution by promising $1m daily to randomly selected signatories.
The defendants denied the allegations.
Musk founded America Pac to support Donald Trump as he successfully ran in November 2024 for a second US presidency.
A federal judge in June said Musk – the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX as well as the owner of the social media platform X – must testify in the lawsuits.

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital and returns to Vatican after lung cancer surgery
keyFacts: Pope Leo XIV left Gemelli Hospital on Saturday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous nodule from his right lung.
Doctors confirmed the 71-year-old pope has lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.
The Holy See Press Office stated that Pope Leo XIV will lead the Angelus prayer from the Vatican tomorrow.
body: Pope Leo XIV left Gemelli Hospital in Rome on Saturday, four days after the removal of a cancerous nodule in his lung.

Doctors from the hospital told reporters that Leo, 71, had resumed certain normal activities after the surgery while staying at Gemelli. The operation confirmed the pope has lung adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

“Following the doctors’ assessment this morning, Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today from Gemelli Hospital, where he was hospitalized for surgery on his right lung,” the Holy See Press Office said in a statement. “He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican. Tomorrow, he will lead the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment.”
Leo was considered “fit for discharge from the hospital” by his personal physician and surgeon after undergoing blood tests and an X-ray of his chest.

This picture, released by Vatican Media on Friday, Oct. 16, 2026, shows Pope Leo XIV, flanked by his personal secretary, Monsignor Edgard Iván Rimaycuna Inga, left, celebrating Mass at the Agostino Gemelli Polyclinic in Rome, where he is recovering after having cancer removed from his right lung. (Vatican Media via AP)

The pope held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, during which he spoke with Putin about his desire to continue dialogue between the Roman Catholic Church and the Russian Orthodox Church. The pope also expressed concern about the Ukrainian city of Oleshky in the Kherson region, which is facing a severe humanitarian crisis according to the United Nations, seeking a truce to allow for the flow of aid and the evacuation of 1,700 trapped civilians.
WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT POPE LEO XIV’S LUNG CANCER DIAGNOSIS
The Vatican also released images on Friday showing Leo celebrating Mass in a hospital chapel, presiding over the liturgy and distributing Communion to hospital staff and Vatican security officers.

These activities and the quick discharge from the hospital demonstrate positive signs of the pope’s health. However, doctors are still waiting for results from tests analyzing the cancer and whether any further treatment is necessary.

articles.headline: Company Behind GTA-Like Samson Goes Bankrupt Six Months After Release
keyFacts: Swedish developer Liquid Swords has filed for bankruptcy following an order issued by the Stockholm District Court on October 12, according to reports.
The studio's first and only game, Samson, launched with technical issues and poor reviews, and about 30 developers have reportedly not been paid since August.
The assigned administrator has put Liquid Swords and its assets up for sale with a bidding window closing on October 21.
body: Liquid Swords, the Swedish developer and publisher behind the recently released GTA-like Samson, has filed for bankruptcy following an order issued by the Stockholm District Court.

Liquid Swords was founded by former Avalanche Studios co-founder Christofer Sundberg, who oversaw the development of all four Just Cause games during his time at the studio. Following Liquid Swordsâ founding in 2020, the studioâs first and only title, Samson, was released to Steam on April 8, 2026.

Samson was released to less-than-stellar reviews and is currently sitting at a score of 51 percent on Metacritic. Critics and players primarily took issue with Samsonâs litany of bugs and performance-related issues at launch, which resulted in an impassioned apology letter from Sundberg on Steam. Sundberg described the gameâs state at launch as âunacceptable,â and vowed to address its âgame-breaking bugs and performance issuesâ in future patches. To Liquid Swords’ credit, Samson has received several updates since release.

As reported by Swedish news site Breakit (via Gametalk), the Stockholm District Court issued the bankruptcy order against Liquid Swords on October 12. According to Gametalkâs report, Liquid Swords employed close to 30 developers, all of whom have reportedly not been paid since August 2026.

However, the team has still been hard at work over the past two months. Samson received an update on Steam on October 8, and it was released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles last month, on September 21.

Whether the game will continue to receive updates is still up in the air, as Breakit reports that the administrator assigned to Liquid Swords, Cirio Law, has already put the developer and its assets, including Samson, up for sale. The bidding window closes on October 21, at which point we should have a clearer idea of Samsonâs future.
Liquid Swords and its founder and COO, Christofer Sundberg, have seemingly not addressed the bankruptcy order on any of their social media accounts.

articles.headline: From handyman to House history: HVAC mogul Joe Strada pushes trade schools, business mindset in Florida race
keyFacts: Republican Joe Strada is running for Florida's eleventh congressional district and could become the wealthiest person to ever serve in the House.
Strada stated he is campaigning to reduce government regulations and promote trade school education as an alternative to college debt.
Strada will face Democrat James Pericola in Florida's general congressional election in three weeks.
body: If Republican Joe Strada wins Florida's eleventh congressional district in three weeks, he will likely be the wealthiest individual to ever hold a seat in the US House of Representatives.
It's an impressive trajectory for a man from humble beginnings who got his start fixing equipment in a bowling alley, but always had a zest for learning, building, and working with his hands.

Strada, whose HVAC, electrical and plumbing company employs roughly 4,000 people across 13 states, told Fox News Digital that his journey from handyman to wealthy entrepreneur embodies the American Dream but that neither his fortune nor his business success defines him.
PULLING BILLIONS FROM HARVARD TO FUND TRADE SCHOOLS? HERE’S WHAT PEOPLE ARE SAYING ABOUT TRUMP’S LATEST MOVE

"How about that? Just the kid, a handyman in a bowling alley, fixing things that break…and now I'm blessed to have a business that's in 13 states, thousands of people that work for me. It's been a blessing and, I'm able to live the American dream.

"But it's difficult. It was difficult with the headwinds and the rules and regulations that come out of Washington, D.C. And it was very challenging …It should be difficult, but not this challenging."
Strada wants everyone to be able to benefit from the American capitalist system that brought him great success:

"You know, as a business owner, I realized and recognized all the problems that Washington, D.C. is causing. All the rules and regulations that are impacting families, small business owners all across the country. And I finally said, we need a different type of person in Washington, DC .

"We have enough lobbyists, politicians and attorneys there. It's time to have a business-minded person that knows how to fix things that could go to Washington, and solve problems for the real, you know, real problems for the American people."
Strada is on a nationwide mission to pitch young people on the value of the trades, and suggests it's a worthy alternative to racking up massive student loans:

"The word of trade is really starting to spread now. Trades people, young people just want to be successful. Sometimes they don't know there's an opportunity in the trades. You come to my company, you don't know how to spell AC, you don't know what end of the screwdriver to hold, but you're paid the very first day. We train you. We give you a career that will support yourself and your family the rest of your life.

"You don't have a $250,000 student debt, and you're able to be successful… And my objective, not just with my company, it's across the country. I'm working with trade schools and high schools everywhere. I'm talking to young people all over our country to come into the trades because it's a great opportunity to live your version of the American dream."
As Strada's HVAC company was growing throughout the country, a labor shortage prompted a serious challenge, and a major shift in business strategy:

"The most difficult challenge was we had the opportunity to grow, and we didn't have enough labor. So I had to develop a program to teach people the trade. So we could grow, and we've been fortunate: we're in 13 states now and 4,000 people that work with us. We never would have done that if we didn't develop our own training program.
"I couldn't wait for the government to come and solve my problem. I'm a business guy who solves problems and I had to go develop a training program for young people."
Strada argues that people on government assistance should also take a serious look at the trades, suggesting we have a large untapped labor pool within our own borders:

"The border had to be closed , and we did a great job keeping all the criminals out of our country. And as far as getting more workers, we have Americans that want to work. We have plenty of people sitting at home getting a government paycheck. Let's get them to work.
"Some of them are just lazy and don't want to work, others just need the opportunity and the push to say, 'this is easy, let's get into a trade, let's learn a business.'
TRUMP-BACKED GOP CANDIDATE WHO OUSTED SCANDAL-PLAGUED INCUMBENT WARNS AGAINST 'NEVER-ENDING WAR' WITH IRAN
"I've have plenty of people that turned out to be an entrepreneur. They've opened their own business, and I'm very happy and gratified when I'm helping people."
Hard work is at the foundation of Strada's success, and he argues an inherent part of that economic success is bringing others along:

"You know, most people think when you're successful, it was handed to you. I got to tell you, David, I'm proud of the hard work my father did, but it was tough growing up. We were fortunate, we had a swimming pool, but it was mainly, a lot of times it was green because we couldn't afford chlorine. It was the best Marco Polo pool in the neighborhood.

"I started with nothing. It's just hard work. The passion and drive to want to be successful, to achieve goals. And it's always about everybody wins. My employees have to win. My customers have to win, the company has to win and that's the position I like to be in is to be able to help sit at a table, moderate those kinds of things and execute those results."
Ultimately, Strada downplays the importance of money, and emphasizes character, while revealing that his greatest motivation in life was born from a family tragedy:

"I wake up every day the same person I was when I was 12 years old that I am today. I've been blessed to be wealthy. I worked hard. I don't apologize for it…But you know, money is just a number. My perspective is everybody puts their head on the pillow at the end of the night. And when you put your head on your pillow, what do you stand for? What's the character of who you are?

"How much money you have…How many zeros you have and where the decimal point is on your bank account? None of that matters. What kind of character are you? I strive every day to do the right thing. For my God, my son in heaven who looks down at me, I want to make him proud. Every decision I make is to make him proud of me, and I do the best I can every single day."
Strada's son, Joe Strada, was an innocent bystander killed by a stray bullet in Lake Mary, FL, during a gunfight outside a shopping center in 2018.
Finally, Strada promises to be a powerful voice for tradeschools if he is elected to Congress next month.

"Well, first of all, I would love to have my name on the SAVE Act and put it into law. That's the first thing. I also think our trade schools are so important: to treat our trade school just like we have our Ivy League colleges.

"We're funding our Ivy league colleges billions and billions of dollars and we're graduating unhirable people that, some of them, hate America. I think the trade schools need more support from our government and treat them just like the universities."
Strada will face off in the general election against Democrat James Pericola, a Clinton administration official.

articles.headline: The Blood of Dawnwalker's first major update will add directional animal petting and a new story mode that's easier than the previous story mode
keyFacts: Developer Rebel Wolves announced that update 1.1 for the vampire RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker will introduce directional animal petting for cats and dogs.
The update adds a new, easier Story mode with combat assists for players who want to focus on the narrative.
Update 1.1 will also include an item to reset and reallocate skill points, alongside improved combat targeting and other minor changes.
body: I've nothing against games that feature simulated animal petting, but it's never been something I've considered buying a game specifically for. Sure, it's nice when your character can stroke a virtual dog or fuss with a clump of polygons shaped like a cat, but it rarely amounts to more than a canned animation. That said, I am suddenly more tempted to shell out on The Blood of Dawnwalker, as Rebel Wolves has announced that the next update to its vampire RPG will introduce "directional animal petting".

The Blood of Dawnwalker already features a directional combat system in the vein of Kingdom Come: Deliverance. And this system lies at the heart of the animal petting being added to version 1.1 of the vampire RPG—according to an update the developer posted on X: "What happens when you merge a directional combat system with an ability to pet dogs and cats?" Rebel Wolves asked. "Directional. Animal. Petting."

Sadly, Rebel Wolves didn't provide any further detail about this system. But it did offer plenty of insight into what else is coming with update 1.1. Aside from being able to stroke cats at different angles, perhaps the most significant addition is a new Story mode. This will feature an "additional combat assist" for players who aren't interested in mastering the game's swordplay, letting them focus mainly on enjoying the narrative and making decisions. It's worth noting this will not replace the existing Story mode outright. That difficulty setting will still exist, but under the new name of "Forgiving."

Elsewhere, The Blood of Dawnwalker will now allow players to rework their abilities through the Draught of Mind Rebirth, which gives you back the points you've allocated into the RPG's various skill trees and lets you spend them elsewhere. That's it for major new features, but smaller changes coming in 1.1 include improved combat targeting, better traversal, in-game camera tweaks, and updates to the RPG's FrameGen tech.

In total, Rebel Wolves promise 1100 changes coming to The Blood of Dawnwalker. It's unlikely any of these will relate to the game's controversial time mechanic, even though the studio has said this system might not feature in the sequel. And a sequel to The Blood of Dawnwalker is coming. Rebel Wolves is already working on it after the first game sold 1 million copies in its first three days on sale.

articles.headline: Steam's Achievement Sets beta aims to stop new content breaking your completion status
keyFacts: Valve announced a beta test for Steam Achievement Sets, a feature that allows developers to group game achievements into distinct collections.
The new feature aims to prevent new content updates from breaking completion status for players who have already finished the base game.
Valve stated it will continue making improvements during the beta as developers begin implementing the new tools for supported games.
body: Valve is beta testing Steam Achievement Sets, a feature that lets developers group a game's achievements into collections.

In an announcement, the company said that games "live longer than ever, continuing to receive updates through new DLC, expansions, and seasons", but that achievements added with new content "can be hard to discover and can accidentally break the completion status of players who have already finished the game".

That's why developers can now specify the number of sets and the purpose of each "to match their game's specific needs", so one game might group its achievements into single-player and multiplayer groups, while another could use eight class-based sets. Players still unlock achievements as usual, and Steam then sorts what they've unlocked into the developer-created sets, which Valve says makes it "easier to see what you have completed and to find other related achievements you can unlock next".
Each set has its own progress bar, and completing one adds a "set complete" trophy to the player's profile. If new achievements are later added to a set, completion is "preserved".

Developers can also create new sets as a game grows, which Valve says makes it "easy for returning players to see what new things they can unlock, while also preserving their prior completion status until they play again".

There are two types of set. Base Game sets "contain achievements that can be earned by all players who play a game", with progress and trophies shown in blue, while DLC sets group achievements that can only be earned once additional content has been bought and are shown in purple.
Interestingly, DLC achievements "are not included in your overall game progress until you have access to the content", so players can track what they have unlocked in new content separately.

Developers can also archive individual achievements or entire sets, which Valve says could suit "season-based games or enabling time-limited holiday achievements". Players who had already unlocked an archived achievement or set "will still see it on their profile", but archived achievements "won't show up on the profile pages of users who missed the unlock nor block their progress toward completing a set or game".

Alongside the sets comes an updated achievements page, reachable from the Games List on the web and from games in the Steam Library, and Search now has filters for specific sets and for locked or unlocked achievements. Players can also compare their progress with "up to three friends, including rare achievements, completed sets, and progress in DLC sets".

Elsewhere, the Perfect Games tab is now called Completed and "expands to show both completed games and games with completed achievement sets", games played via Family Sharing now appear in the Games List, and friends who played a game that way are eligible for friend comparison. Store and Library pages will also show if a game has achievement sets.

The beta is available to players and developers, and Valve says it will "continue making improvements during the beta", adding that "as developers begin using the new tools, you'll start seeing these changes appear for supported games".

Games that have already added achievement sets are Against the Storm, Age of Wonders 4, American Truck Simulator, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Crusader Kings 3, Dredge, Euro Truck Simulator 2, Forza Horizon 5, Flock Around, He is Coming, LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, Left 4 Dead 2, Portal 2, PowerWash Simulator, PowerWash Simulator 2, Team Fortress 2, and Victoria 3.

Valve's PC digital store and social platform set a new user concurrent record last Sunday, clocking up a staggering 43,505,724 users. Meanwhile, Epic Games isn't lifting its foot off the gen-AI pedal, having vibe-coded a new Epic Games Launcher in an attempt to outrun Steam, by far the most popular digital games marketplace on PC.

articles.headline: Plug-in solar is legal in these 10 states now – how it could save you money
keyFacts: Ten states, beginning with Utah, have legalized backyard and plug-in solar systems for residential use.
Plug-in solar lowers electric bills, but utility opposition and home wiring concerns keep it illegal in many states.
About two dozen states are considering legalization bills, with some advancing and others stalled until the 2027 legislative session.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Multiple states are working to legalize backyard solar setups.
- After Utah, nine other states have legalized it, or are working on bills for plug-in solar.
- 24 other states are stalled but already working on legislation.

Plug-in solar systems are easy to set up and can save consumers money on their power bills, but they’re still illegal in many states. Utah was the first to legalize backyard and plug-in solar, but other states have since caught on, and more are working on their own pathway to legalization.

As we’ve covered before, these plug-in solar setups (also commonly called “backyard solar”) are plug-and-play systems consisting of one or more solar panels, an inverter, and a battery. The system connects to a home’s standard 120-volt outlet, automatically routing solar-generated electricity from the battery to the nearest running appliance.
More from ZDNET
What states have legalized plug-in solar?

Ten states have already legalized backyard and plug-in solar systems, so residents there can already purchase and install systems like the EcoFlow Stream in their homes. Here’s the current status of the states that have already successfully passed legislation, legalizing such devices for consumer use.
Data sourced from Solar.com.
What states are working to legalize plug-in solar?

About two dozen states are still in the process of legalizing plug-in solar. Some bills have stalled until the next legislative session reconvenes in 2027, while others are going through committee hearings.

Balcony solar bills H.5175 and S3143 are advancing in Massachusetts, and the SUNNY Act is pending governor approval in New York. Bills in other states like Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, and Washington, DC have reached committee hearings.

Most states have stalled plug-in solar bills until the next legislative session in 2027, including Alaska, Arizona, Delaware, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, North Carolina, and Oklahoma.

Unfortunately, plug-in solar bills have failed in Georgia, New Mexico, Oregon, Washington, and Wyoming, so if you live in one of those states, these kinds of devices are technically illegal to operate. This doesn’t mean that it won’t eventually clear the legislative slate in these states, but lawmakers will need to file a new bill to reintroduce them after making necessary revisions.
Can I set up my solar panels if my state legalizes plug-in solar?
Whether you can immediately set up your balcony solar panels or not after the systems are legalized in your state will depend on your home situation.

Generally speaking, the bills in question focus on preventing utility companies from blocking plug-in solar projects. These bills can’t preempt bans on these systems by landlords or HOAs, though supplementary bills have been introduced in some states to include protections for HOAs and landlords.
Why is plug-in solar illegal?

Plug-in solar is illegal because the electrical systems in traditional American homes aren’t designed to receive power from a standard wall outlet. Rooftop solar systems are professionally installed and designed so the energy harvested by the panels flows through a circuit breaker and into your outlets. Plug-in solar, in turn, introduces electricity directly into an outlet, bypassing the electrical panel.

In a plug-in solar setup, nearby appliances draw energy supplied by the breaker and the solar inverter, but the wiring could carry more current than the breaker alone would allow before it trips. But it’s not solely about safety.

Installing your own solar panels means less reliance on local utilities. These companies are the biggest regulatory obstacle for plug-in or balcony solar setups. Their rules and regulations on solar energy are designed for rooftop panels, not plug-and-play systems, so legislation should push utility companies to change that.

There’s also the elephant in the room: utilities would make less money off their services if plug-in solar becomes widely popular. When consumers purchase less electricity, they contribute less to grid costs.

articles.headline: 7 Crazy Movie Premises That Actually Worked
keyFacts: The article highlights several famous films with unusual premises that successfully defied standard storytelling conventions.
Films discussed include Dr. Strangelove, Who Framed Roger Rabbit, It’s a Wonderful Life, Being John Malkovich, and The Raid: Redemption.
The upcoming film Whalefall is based on Daniel Kraus's novel and tells the story of a man swallowed by a whale.
body: “A young man is swallowed by a whale while searching for his father’s remains deep in the ocean.”

That is the elevator pitch for Whalefall , starring Austin Abrams (Resident Evil) and co-written by Daniel Kraus and director Brian Duffield (No One Will Save You). Set for release on October 16, the film is based on Kraus’ 2023 novel, inspired by a viral video of kayakers seemingly being swallowed by a whale . Whalefall’s central conceit is one writers and directors are challenged by, and often dream of, because it raises the questions: Can I pull this off? And how can I make this work? In other words, the absolutely bonkers premise is fertile ground for real creative risk and opportunity.
Read our Whalefall Review

Of course, Whalefall isn’t the first or only film to take a big leap. Throughout cinema history, bold filmmakers have swung for the fences and connected. Too many for just one list, in fact. Children of Men, Groundhog Day, Parasite, The Truman Show, Tie Me Up! Tie Me Down!, Spirited Away, The City of Lost Children, The Stepford Wives, Inside Out, Poor Things, Everything Everywhere All at Once, and many more could easily have made this list. The following is a small sample of films that successfully stepped out of standard storytelling boxes.
Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb (1964)
“Gentlemen, you can’t fight in here! This is the War Room!”

Positive that communists are poisoning the “precious bodily fluids” of the American populace, General Jack D. Ripper launches an unauthorized nuclear attack on the U.S.S.R., triggering an increasingly farcical crisis which culminates in a dunce's doomsday, an apocalypse driven by insane idiots and a Nazi.

One of cinema’s great political satires, Dr. Strangelove opened in 1964, about a year and a half after the Cuban Missile Crisis, when the world held its breath, wondering if we really were going to self-destruct. Stripping away the reasoned tones that politicians of the day used to discuss nightmare scenarios, Dr. Strangelove captures the powerless fear of a populace, and exposes geopolitics for what it so often is: utterly unhinged and stupid (possibly drunk), and treating mass casualty as if it is a child’s game to win or lose.

The film cost $1.8 million to make and earned more than $9 million at the domestic box office . Though it was shut out at the Academy Awards with four nominations and zero wins, it earned several nominations and four wins at the BAFTAs, including Best British Film and Best Film from Any Source. Upon release, reviewers were polarized: some found genius in the dark comedy, while others were disturbed by its treatment of the very real threat of nuclear war. Over time, it has become director Stanley Kubrick’s highest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes, at 98%, and was deemed so influential that the National Film Registry selected it as one of its first 25 films in 1989. Director Michael Mann went so far as to say he wasn’t really interested in movies until he saw Dr. Strangelove. It remains a standard-bearer for satire. It captures essential truth, if not (necessarily) objective reality. As for reality, military officials criticized the film upon release, yet, coincidentally or not, made internal changes that mapped to the vulnerabilities Dr. Strangelove exposed .
Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988)

In a world where sentient cartoons live alongside humans, Eddie Valiant – an alcoholic private detective with a vendetta against toons – is hired to investigate a sultry cartoon femme fatale, Jessica Rabbit, who may be cuckolding her stuttering rabbit husband, Roger. When her alleged lover is found dead, Valiant is forced to protect the unruly rabbit and drawn into a sinister toon conspiracy.

Roger Rabbit was a hit with audiences and critics alike right out of the gate, and stands at 96% on Rotten Tomatoes. Praised for its visionary storytelling, which mixes zany cartoon comedy with classic noir tropes, and for its revolutionary technical achievement, the film left viewers spellbound. Though live action and animation had been integrated before, audiences had never seen anything quite like Roger Rabbit. Bob Hoskins’ emotional performance as the detective on a redemption arc was lauded, particularly in that he was acting, essentially, with empty space for much of the film. Kathleen Turner’s rich voice cemented Jessica Rabbit as an iconic animated character.

Made for $50 million ($70 million by some estimates ), the film earned just over $350 million worldwide. It had six Academy Award nominations and three wins (plus a Special Achievement Academy Award for animation direction) and was added to the National Film Registry in 2016 . Thanks to executive producer Steven Spielberg’s negotiations, it wowed audiences by bringing together animated characters from both Warner Bros. and Disney. Along with The Little Mermaid, it also helped usher in the Disney Animation renaissance. Similar releases followed, including 1992’s Cool World, starring Brad Pitt as a human detective and Kim Basinger as a cartoon femme fatale named Holli Would, and 1996’s Space Jam, which teamed Michael Jordan with the Looney Tunes. Arguably, the film that’s come closest to capturing Roger Rabbit’s appeal is the recent Coyote vs. Acme, but, for many, nothing truly touches the 1988 classic. According to director Robert Zemeckis , Stanley Kubrick deeply appreciated the film and, while watching it, searched for the hidden “sleight of hand” movie magic that made it all come together, before ultimately realizing it was “just an incredible amount of backbreaking work” that made Roger Rabbit possible.
It’s a Wonderful Life (1946)

A suicidal man embittered by career sacrifices and disappointments, and facing ruin and jail, meets with a fledgling angel (eager to advance in his own vocation) on Christmas Eve. In order for the latter to win the promotion he wants (get his wings), he must convince the former that there’s more to life than work and material success, and that his impact on the world has been sizable and good, despite all evidence to the contrary.

Perhaps that’s a hyperbolic synopsis, but the fact is, while director Frank Capra’s holiday favorite may be considered a sentimental classic today, audiences at the time of its release seemingly weren’t ready for this unorthodox take on Christmas cheer. Though it received mixed to somewhat positive reviews (particularly praising Jimmy Stewart’s lead performance) and ultimately earned five Oscar nominations, it won no Academy Awards beyond a Technical Achievement Award and was a box-office flop. RKO, the studio that released the film, reported a $525,000 loss . But It’s a Wonderful Life did nearly gain notoriety – via controversy , when the FBI flagged it to the House Un-American Activities Committee (which was investigating potential Communist influences in Hollywood), noting anti-capitalist undertones (as the film’s banker was the most hated character). Alas, it couldn’t even get negative PR, as the committee decided not to bring the creators in to testify.

The film was largely overlooked in the decades that followed. Capra himself was taken aback , if pleasantly so, when it finally found its audience. The full story is more complex, but, effectively, a clerical fluke meant the film’s copyright lapsed in 1974 , making it cheap to run on television during the holidays, which it did for many years. The copyright situation was eventually resolved through the rights in the underlying story and music. By then, it had become a beloved standard. Distance gave viewers space to see what was always there. Audiences and critics alike recognized the special magic in the strange mix of sentimentality, whimsy, very real and deeply painful human despair, and the essential truth that we all desire to know, truly know, that our lives matter. In a 1999 essay, film critic Roger Ebert said this film belonged to a category that could withstand indefinite viewings: “Like great music, they improve with familiarity.” Years after it opened and flopped, It’s a Wonderful Life became a holiday television staple, drawing millions of viewers for its Christmas Eve broadcasts, and now holds a 94% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.
Being John Malkovich (1999)

While working a bland office job, struggling street puppeteer Craig Schwartz stumbles upon a portal to actor John Malkovich’s mind, where he can experience the celebrity’s life for exactly 15 minutes before being spat back out onto the New Jersey Turnpike. He and the co-worker he’s in love with start a business charging $200 per person for a visit into the actor’s experience. Eventually, multiple characters battle to permanently take over Malkovich’s life, creating a series of betrayals, identity crises, opportunities found and then lost, and the annihilation of the self.

Charlie Kaufman’s surreal screenplay is arguably one of the biggest swings on this list. Malkovich himself initially worried it would bomb , and the script circulated Hollywood with no takers. One exec reportedly asked, “Why the f— can’t it be Being Tom Cruise?” However, director Francis Ford Coppola got the script to his daughter’s then-boyfriend, Spike Jonze, who directed it and helped get it produced. The movie opened to great acclaim, presumably stunning skeptical industry players. It has a 94% on Rotten Tomatoes, with Roger Ebert calling it “endlessly inventive,” adding that “[it] has ideas enough for half a dozen films.” Critics celebrated its inventiveness, layered themes, and ensemble performances from John Cusack, Cameron Diaz, Catherine Keener, and, of course, John Malkovich.

It cost $13 million to produce and went on to earn either $23 million or $32 million globally (depending on the source). It didn’t win any of its three Oscar nominations, but it won Best First Feature and Best First Screenplay at the Independent Spirit Awards. It appears on multiple “best of” lists, including Empire magazine ’s 500 Greatest Movies of All Time and the Writers Guild of America’s 101 Greatest Screenplays Ever Written . Like Kaufman’s other films (two of which, Adaptation and Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, nearly made this list), Being John Malkovich demonstrates what is possible when you follow even the most nonsensical threads of imagination.
The Raid: Redemption (2011)

A SWAT team, trapped in a hostile high-rise, must battle its way up the stairs to capture a crime lord; end of story. The Raid is unique on this list in that the plot isn’t a fit of wild imagination; rather, it has almost no plot at all. It has a premise and wall-to-wall unparalleled fight sequences. It grips the viewer and doesn’t let go for the entire runtime, leaving audiences breathless and feeling like they, too, just punched their way to victory. It’s exhilarating, near-perfect action that other films have chased for 15 years.

The Indonesian actioner cost $1.1 million to make, according to director Gareth Evans , and earned over $9 million worldwide at the box office, plus another $10 million in U.S. DVD and Blu-ray sales alone. No traditional narrative necessary. It stands at 87% on Rotten Tomatoes and performed well during its film festival run – Evans said he was “blown away” by the reception at the Toronto International Film Festival. The movie became an industry reference point, with John Wick director Chad Stahelski telling Den of Geek that directors unfamiliar with fight choreography would specifically ask for something like The Raid, among other iconic action films. Yayan Ruhian and Cecep Arif Rahman, two actors from The Raid franchise, were ultimately cast as two of Keanu Reeves’ adversaries in John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum. The film is a beloved fan favorite and cultural touchstone for best-in-class hand-to-hand action.
Get Out (2017)

On a trip to visit his girlfriend’s parents, a talented photographer makes a horrific discovery: a group of Obama-voting white suburbanites has found a way to use misophonia-inducing teaspoons, hypnosis, and surgery to transplant the consciousness of wealthy, older white people into young, Black kidnappees, whose own psyches are sent into a purgatorial “sunken place.”

Director Jordan Peele’s groundbreaking debut became an instant cultural phenomenon, blending social commentary with genuinely entertaining horror. The director builds real suspense, psychological terror, and tension-releasing humor into a film that lays systemic racism bare through a deeply imaginative metaphor. It has a 98% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Peele made Academy Awards history as the first Black writer to win an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay. Get Out was also nominated for Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor (Daniel Kaluuya). In late 2021, the WGA named the script the #1 Greatest Screenplay of the 21st Century (So Far). Financially, Get Out was a juggernaut, making $255 million worldwide on a $4.5 million budget, and breaking The Blair Witch Project’s domestic record as the highest-grossing debut film based on an original screenplay.

Director Christopher Nolan had this to say of Get Out: “How often do you get the experience of seeing something that you have no idea where it's going to go, and then it goes somewhere far more interesting than you ever imagined?"
Barbie (2023)

Faced with an unexpected existential crisis, Barbie must travel from the utopia of Barbieland into the “real” world to find and soothe the unhappy person playing with her so that she can once again experience the sweet oblivion of not thinking about death, or life, or meaning… and bask in thighs free of cellulite. Ken tags along and, upon discovering patriarchy, starts an uprising when he returns to Barbieland.

The overall sentiment when Barbie debuted was that this movie absolutely should not work . Yet it surprised and delighted audiences with its mix of subversive humor (that both acknowledges and reframes Barbie’s cultural impact), standout performances from producer and star Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling (as Barbie and Ken), and an optimistic core. It inspired multiple viewings for many audience members, some of whom came to theaters decked out in celebratory pink. Doctor Strange director Scott Derrickson said the film was one of his two favorites that year, and an example of IP “treated with true brilliance,” calling it an “extraordinary movie on every level.”

Set against Oppenheimer in the summer’s race for dominance, affectionately known as Barbenheimer, the film catapulted to box office success. It was a risk for both Mattel and Warner Bros., who distributed it. They trusted co-writer and largely indie director Greta Gerwig, who’d never helmed a film this big, with an iconic but controversial doll and a $128 million budget. The bet paid off: Barbie earned a staggering $1.4 billion worldwide at the box office , holds an 88% on Rotten Tomatoes, and received eight Oscar nominations, winning Best Original Song for “What Was I Made For?” and taking home the first-ever Golden Globe for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement. Ultimately, the film’s pathos stayed with viewers. Barbie is the picture of stagnant perfection, so who better to take a messy journey where triumph lies in living the most mundane moments of a human life?
What are your favorite crazy movie premises that somehow worked? Let’s discuss in the comments!

articles.headline: How to get Alucard’s Sword and Shield in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse
keyFacts: Players can obtain Alucard's Sword and Shield in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse by reaching Alucard's Tower in the Main Hall.
Reaching the area requires the Double Jump ability to travel through the Mirror of Life in the Entrance Corridor.
To open the shrine path, players must destroy five blue flames along the path using their Arcane whip.
body: Alucard’s Sword and Shield is one of the best weapons available in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, bit it won’t be handed out to you. Instead, you’ll need to unlock the weapon by obtaining it on your adventure.
In this guide, I will help you out by listing its exact location.
How to unlock Alucard’s Sword and Shield in Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse

First, you have to complete the game until you reach Alucard’s Tower in the Main Hall. This is the main location of the weapon. To get the Shield and Sword, we will be heading to the top part of the area, above the library’s entrance.

Screenshot by Destructoid So, how do you reach the tower? First, go to the Entrance Corridor’s Mirror of Life, and use your whip on the painting to reach the nearby glowing red door. You can only get this part done if you have unlocked the Double Jump movement ability.

Screenshot by Destructoid Next, head to the red door in the Grand Hall. There will be challenges along the way, and a part of the path will be created with switches. Keep heading upwards, and you’ll come across an Alucard portrait.

Screenshot by Destructoid When you try to reach the upper level, you’ll find the door blocked by five blue flames. Find them along around the path to the tower, and use your Arcane whip to destroy them all.
Finally, the locked path will be open, allowing you to gain access to the shrine. Interact with it to reach the spot where Alucard’s Sword and Shield can be obtained from the wall.
